business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Common Law: English common law as applied in Alberta, overlaid by federal and provincial statutes (Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9; federal AML/CFT and sanctions statutes). Quebec civil law does not apply to Alberta.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended by the 2007 and 2008 Protocols — Article IV(7) fiscally-transparent pass-through treatment for shareholders of Alberta ULCs
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), EU–Canada (investment and cross-border services, provisionally applied)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1 (Terrorist Financing) and Part XII.2 (Proceeds of Crime); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA) — Unlimited Liability Corporation regime and ss 18.1–18.3 (Register of Individuals with Significant Control); Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp); Canada–US Tax Convention, Article IV(7).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the UBO's/director's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded 11 January 2024; competent authorities: Global Affairs Canada for federal documents, Service Alberta / Alberta Queen's Printer for Alberta provincial documents; foreign documents require apostille of the state of origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or certified corporate extract for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction companies registry or licensed corporate service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization at a Canadian embassy or consulate where the issuing jurisdiction is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Alberta incorporation agent and registered-office service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account conduct and identity of the UBO

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against (1) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and all persons listed under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (2) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (3) the OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, applied as a prudent cross-border banking standard; and (4) commercial PEP databases covering foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and heads of international organizations. Verification must cover identity, address, source of funds, and source of wealth of every director, shareholder, and UBO. The present data-center colocation scope (ISIC 6209) is a Low_Risk_Standard, non-licensed activity under the PCMLTFA regime; however, the ULC must still maintain its internal ISC register and respond to lawful government and law-enforcement disclosure demands, and enhanced due diligence becomes mandatory if the entity later engages in regulated activities such as money remittance or virtual-currency dealing.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance_note: Alberta ABCA requires an 'individual with significant control' (ISC) register; disclosure to the registry is not public, but the register must be produced to the Canada Revenue Agency, FINTRAC, and law-enforcement bodies on lawful demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — online Corporate Registry system at alta.registries.gov.ab.ca (accessible directly and through authorized Registry Agents); NUANS name search reports are mandatory and obtained via the same system or accredited NUANS providers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in English or French or a transliterated/translated form accompanied by a certified translation; it must be distinctive and not confusing under ABCA ss 10–11. A statutory legal element is required — for an Alberta ULC the name must end with 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or the abbreviation 'ULC' (French equivalent: 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' / 'SRI'). Numerals, initials, and punctuation are permissible, but the NUANS report must demonstrate no conflict with existing corporate names, registered trade names, or trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Loan Company, Insurance, Assurance — require federal OSFI regulatory approval before provincial acceptance
Royal, Crown, Government, Governmental, Federal — imply royal or governmental patronage and require ministerial consent
Canada, Canadian — restricted where the name implies a federal crown corporation or misleads as to corporate status
University, College, Institute, Academy — require sectoral regulatory consent
Co-operative, Condominium, Credit Union — regulated statutory terms
Exchange, Clearing House, Securities — imply regulated market infrastructure
Data Center, Colocation, Hosting, Telecom — permitted as descriptive tokens but must accurately describe the business actually to be carried on in Alberta
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation under the ABCA is valid for 90 days and may be renewed only by filing a new reservation application with a fresh NUANS report before expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant or its registered agent may file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, within 30 days of the rejection notice, rebutting the confusion analysis under ABCA s 10(3) with evidence of distinctiveness, registered trademark rights, or consent letters from holders of similar names. An adverse reconsideration decision may be appealed to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by application for judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the statutory registered office: Alberta requires a street address in Alberta where process and corporate documents can be served, and a licensed registered-agent or virtual-office address satisfies the ABCA provided physical receipt and forwarding of process and mail is contractually guaranteed. However, the virtual office cannot serve as the colocation data center's actual operating address and does not establish commercial substance for GST/HST registration, income-tax residency, or Canada–US treaty benefit purposes; the ULC must maintain genuine operational presence at the physical data-center site in Alberta.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 0.05 (5%) — Low. The Alberta Corporate Registry conducts document-based compliance and does not routinely perform unannounced inspections. Physical verification would arise only upon a FINTRAC inquiry, law-enforcement suspicion, or Canada Revenue Agency audit of the data center's actual operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 ('ABCA'): s. 15 (incorporation), s. 18 (articles), s. 21 (share issuance), s. 101 (registered office), s. 141 (directors). Alberta permits an Unlimited Liability Corporation ('ULC') by declaring unlimited liability in the articles; the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, does not govern this Alberta entity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed online with the Alberta Corporate Registry; Certificate of Incorporation issued upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or capital deposit requirement under the ABCA. Shares may be issued for such lawful consideration as the directors determine, and no pre-funding of share capital is required before incorporation; a mandatory subscription letter is executed by the founding shareholder and shares are issued upon receipt of consideration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscription of the founding shareholder be accepted and that common shares be issued upon receipt of lawful consideration. RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at the address of M/s Corporate Services, Calgary, Alberta, with statutory records maintained thereat. RESOLVED, that the Initial Registered Office Address and Notice of Directors be filed with Alberta Corporate Registry. RESOLVED, that [Name A], [Name B], and [Name C] be appointed President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, respectively. Such appointments take effect immediately and continue until the next annual meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Name Services, Service Alberta (online NUANS portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed corporate name, e.g. 'DATA CENTER & COLOCATION ULC', through an authorized Alberta Corporate Registry Agent. Reserve the approved name for 90 days. The name must include 'ULC', 'Unlimited Liability Company', or the approved abbreviation to satisfy ABCA naming rules for unlimited liability corporations.
required_dossiers: NUANS Corporate Name Search Request form
Non-standard name consent letter (if the name contains non-distinctive or sensitive words)
Authorized agent appointment form (when filed through a registry agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for being confusingly similar or misdescriptive, submit an alternative name request or provide a written consent from the prior name holder; a refused NUANS report can be re-filed by the agent without forfeiting the original search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (legal review and registration section).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 setting out the corporate name, unlimited liability clause, registered office address, share structure, and first directors. Execute the articles before witnesses, notarize incorporator signatures, and pay the CAD 100 state filing fee (plus agent fees). Ensure the registered office is a physical address in Alberta and the director consents are dated and signed.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation
Valid NUANS name search report (issued within 90 days)
Notarized incorporator signatures
Directors' consent to act as first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a correction notice for defective share provisions or an invalid registered office address, revise the Form 1 and re-submit; only the standard amendment fee is payable and the original filing date is preserved where the correction is timely.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles of Incorporation Online with Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online portal (Corporate Registry e-file service).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in through a licensed Alberta Registry Agent, upload the completed Form 1 and supporting appendices, verify the corporate name and registered office address, pay the state fee and e-filing charges, and monitor the filing status until the Certificate of Incorporation is generated.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 Articles of Incorporation (PDF with digital signatures)
NUANS report in searchable format
Registry agent e-service authorization confirmation
Proof of filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the online filing is queried for incomplete documents, contact the Corporate Registry's corporate support desk within 5 business days, provide the missing material, and re-submit; expedited processing (1-hour to same-day) can be purchased to restore the intended formation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and ULC Status Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Certificate and Records Section).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download and print the Certificate of Incorporation and the certified Articles of Incorporation. Verify the Alberta corporate registration number, confirm the unlimited liability designation appears in the articles, and deposit the original certificate in the corporate minute book at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Certified Articles of Incorporation (including ULC unlimited liability clause)
Corporate registration number confirmation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains legal or typographical errors, submit a Form 11 correction request to the Registrar within 30 days; if the certificate is lost, order a True Copy with the raised seal from the Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for CRA Business Number, GST/HST, and Corporate Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online, with Alberta Treasury Board and Finance for provincial tax registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the ULC for a Business Number via CRA's Business Registration Online portal. Select the corporate income tax account and, if annual taxable supplies will exceed CAD 30,000, the GST/HST account. Register for the Alberta corporate income tax account if the entity is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation or where provincial tax registration is triggered. Use NAICS 518210 for data center and hosting activities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office address in Alberta
Directors' legal names and tax identification numbers (SIN or ITIN for non-residents)
Principal business activity description (data center colocation and bare-metal server hosting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA flags a duplicate Business Number or incorrect program account, contact the CRA business tax services desk with the corporate registration number and statutory records; if GST/HST classification is wrong, re-submit the account selection with corrected income statement activity codes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene First Organizational Meeting, Appoint Officers, and Adopt By-Law No. 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal governance; no government filing required for officer appointments, but the annual return must be filed with Alberta Corporate Registry).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting of directors. Adopt By-Law No. 1 covering director indemnity, corporate seal, meeting procedures, and share certificates. Approve the share subscription and allotment, fix the registered office, approve bank signing authorities, and confirm the statutory records location. File the initial annual return in the year of incorporation with the Alberta Corporate Registry.
required_dossiers: By-Law No. 1
Minutes of the first board meeting
Share register and certificate book
Subscription agreement and payment evidence
Annual Return (Alberta Form 4 or online renewal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an item is omitted from the board agenda, cure it by a subsequent written directors' consent resolution; if the annual return filing deadline is missed, file a late annual return with the Registry and pay the standard late-renewal penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Business Licence and Industrial/Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Development and Permits Department (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton as applicable) with Safety Codes Council accredited officers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a development permit application for 'data centre / server room colocation' use, including leasehold floor plans, Tier-3/4 electrical redundancy schematics, cooling equipment specifications, and fire suppression layouts. Obtain the building permit and electrical installation permit before fit-out, and acquire the municipal business licence prior to commencing hosting services.
required_dossiers: Development permit application and leasehold floor plans
Electrical installation permit under the Safety Codes Act
Fire protection and life safety design plan
Municipal business licence application with Certificate of Incorporation
Professional engineer (P.Eng.) floor-loading certificate for server rack areas
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality contests zoning for data centre use, submit a written interpretation request to the Development Authority; if the building permit is refused on structural loading grounds, engage a P.Eng. to issue a supplementary floor-loading certification; if the business licence is denied, request a review by the municipal Business Licensing Committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Safety Codes Council (administered by Alberta Municipal Affairs) in conjunction with the municipal Development Authority having jurisdiction; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas for environmental matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (Data Processing and Hosting) together with Building and Electrical Safety Codes Permits for Tier-3 Data Centre Occupancy

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Not a mandatory EIA activity under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation, Alta Reg 111/1993; data centre colocation is therefore exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment report. A Class I registration or Class II approval under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 may be required for cooling-water intake, wastewater discharge, and stationary combustion sources such as backup B5/diesel generators where regulatory thresholds are met.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Cooling-water and condensate discharges must comply with the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations, SOR/2012-139, where discharge enters fish-bearing waters; Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives apply for backup generator emissions (NOx 200 µg/m³ 1-hour, SO2 171 µg/m³ 1-hour); ozone-depleting substance and HFC refrigerant handling must follow CEPA 1999 Schedule 1 requirements; spent UPS batteries, e-waste, and coolant must be stored, labelled, and transported within 90 days under the Waste Control Regulation, Alta Reg 192/1996.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: approval of automatic fire suppression, HVAC shutdown, and 24/7 monitoring systems under the Alberta Fire Code, with annual certification of fire alarms and suppression equipment. Structural: professional engineer (P.Eng.) floor-loading inspection and certificate for server-rack dead load (minimum 12 kN/m² or 250 kg/m²). Occupational: Alberta OHS clearance certificate covering confined-space entry, electrical safety, hazardous energy control (lockout/tagout), and emergency lighting, in compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Code, Alta Reg 87/2009, Part 22 (Electrical Hazards).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), the federal tax authority, is the sole competent authority for GST/HST and federal corporate income tax and administers the Alberta corporate income tax on behalf of Alberta under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement. Corporate legal registration is completed through the Alberta Corporate Registry (ACR). Digital portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the Alberta ULC under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) through the Alberta Corporate Registry or complete extra-provincial registration; the Alberta corporate registry initiates the CRA Business Number (BN) one-stop process. 2. Confirm the 15-character BN, which includes the 9-digit CRA account number plus a two-character program code suffix (RT = GST/HST; RC = corporate income tax). 3. If the BN is not auto-generated, file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) with the CRA International Tax Services Office; a non-resident applicant must provide a Canadian agent for service of process and, where applicable, a resident representative. 4. Validate or register the GST/HST RT account via My Business Account or Form RC1; non-resident registrants may be required to post security under subsection 298(2) of the Excise Tax Act. 5. File federal T2 and Alberta corporate income tax returns through the CRA; no separate Alberta provincial income tax registration is required because Alberta's corporate tax is assessed and collected by the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) U.S. check-the-box election (Form 8832) to classify the Canadian ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. federal tax purposes, while Canadian domestic law taxes the ULC as a corporation resident in Canada at the entity level. 2) Election under subsection 216(1) of the Income Tax Act permitting a non-resident lessor to file a net-basis Canadian tax return on Canadian-source real property rental income (relevant to colocation-space leases) instead of paying gross Part XIII non-resident withholding tax. 3) Voluntary GST/HST registration election by a small-supplier non-resident under subsection 240(2) of the Excise Tax Act to claim input tax credits. 4) Quick Method of accounting election under section 170 of the Excise Tax Act for eligible GST/HST registrants. 5) No domestic Canadian hybrid-mismatch or check-the-box election exists for the ULC; the Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty and Multilateral Instrument provisions govern the hybrid entity characterization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) - federal value-added tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta has no provincial sales tax or HST, so the effective VAT-type headline rate in Alberta is the federal 5% GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in Canadian taxable supplies (small-supplier threshold under section 148, Excise Tax Act); mandatory GST/HST registration is triggered once a non-resident carrying on business in Canada exceeds CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies either in a single calendar quarter or in the trailing four consecutive calendar quarters, unless the supplies are exclusively zero-rated, in which case registration remains voluntary.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping. GST/HST invoices must contain the prescribed information under subsection 169(3) of the Excise Tax Act and the GST/HST Information Regulations; electronic invoices (EDI, XML, PDF) are valid if they contain such prescribed particulars and are properly retained. GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million must file returns electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or EDI. The voluntary federal Canada E-Invoicing initiative operates on the PEPPOL network for B2G/B2B transactions; there is no transaction-level CRA clearance requirement or mandated tax-authority API. Books and records, including electronic supplier invoices, must be retained for six years and are subject to CRA electronic audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act for (i) goods exported from Canada as part of the supply (sections 1-13) and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident that is not a 'specified non-resident' with a substantial Canadian nexus (sections 7-23). Data-center colocation and rack-space leasing constitute a licence of real property situated in Canada under section 179 of the Excise Tax Act and therefore remain taxable in Canada at 5% GST, not zero-rated, even when supplied to a non-resident. Zero-rating may be claimed only for distinctly separable offshore services (e.g., remote software/cloud-management services to a non-resident without Canadian establishment) and for tangible goods actually exported from Canada. The registrant must obtain and retain contemporaneous documentary proof of export and foreign receipt of payment, with proceeds repatriated within 180 days as an administrative expectation; failure to substantiate results in reassessment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES) or via a CBSA-authorized service provider
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill / cargo movement evidence establishing physical export from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank statement, or foreign-exchange documentation evidencing receipt of proceeds from the non-resident customer
Executed service agreement or master colocation contract identifying the non-resident recipient and the offshore, non-real-property nature of any zero-rated element
Packing list and inventory schedule for exported server hardware or tangible personal property, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may audit and reassess zero-rating claims, with reassessment available beyond the normal four-year limitation period where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established. Penalties include the gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the tax understated or net tax misapplied under sections 280 and 285 of the Excise Tax Act, failure-to-remit penalties, arrears interest, and customs export-form penalties under the Customs Act. Fraudulent claims may also result in criminal prosecution for tax evasion under the Excise Tax Act or the Criminal Code. Retroactive clawback of input tax credits and recharacterization of purported exports as taxable Canadian supplies will follow any unfounded zero-rating claim, and non-resident registrants may lose registration privileges or be subjected to increased security requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada; institutional supervision by Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering oversight by Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Currency Act and Bank of Canada regime. There are no foreign-exchange controls, no central bank approval for outward profit remittances, and no restrictions on holding foreign-currency bank accounts. Dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, and other current payments to non-residents may be freely wired in any convertible currency, subject only to withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada), reduced by applicable tax treaties. Inbound equity or loan capital into the Alberta ULC also requires no exchange-control clearance; however, a non-resident parent's acquisition of control of a Canadian business may require an Investment Canada Act filing (notification or net-benefit application) if specified threshold values are exceeded. The Canadian dollar is determined by a floating exchange rate; authorized Canadian banks may trade USD/CAD and quote spot, forward, swap, and option products without central bank intervention or conversion mandates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline for export receipts. A data center colocation operator may invoice USD or CAD, retain export proceeds in a foreign-currency operating account, hold the funds indefinitely, and convert them at commercial banks when commercially optimal. For AML compliance, Canadian financial institutions must report international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more per transaction to FINTRAC, and any receipt of cash of CAD 10,000 or more triggers a Large Cash Transaction Report. No foreign-exchange surrender certificate or beneficiary-country approval is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Dual capital escrow and operational CAD/USD accounts
Dual capital escrow and operational CAD/USD accounts
Dual capital escrow and operational CAD/USD accounts
Dual capital escrow and operational CAD/USD accounts
Dual capital escrow and operational CAD/USD accounts
Alberta-focused operational account; capital escrow if used for in-province construction
Operational account for Alberta mid-market treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for payment facilitation and treasury visibility; Low as a primary bank-account or capital-escrow solution. Offshore digital EMI providers are not authorized deposit-taking institutions in Canada. Accepting deposits from Canadian ULCs without Bank Act authorization is prohibited; an EMI must be registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and comply with PCMLTFA obligations if it touches Canadian counterparties. Offshore EMIs can provide multi-currency collection accounts, virtual IBANs, and API-driven payment initiation, but settlement finality in CAD requires clearing through a Canadian Schedule I bank with access to Payments Canada (Lynx/ACSS). The legal-entity treasury should therefore hold the ULC's operating liquidity at a Canadian-regulated bank and use EMIs only for non-bank ledger controls, pending settlements, or foreign vendor payments where a correspondent clearing agent is already provided.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Canadian federal statute requires directors to appear physically for account opening. PCMLTFA permits identity verification through credentialed digital identity methods, Canadian credit-file verification, or remote video notarization. In practice, all major Alberta commercial banks require at least one director, officer, or authorized signatory to attend a relationship-manager interview in-person at a Calgary or Edmonton branch for a newly incorporated ULC with non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership, particularly because the ULC has unlimited liability and will transact in high-dollar wire/ACH activity. Remote onboarding is possible for service accounts of existing customers or for purely online transactional products, but a fully remote, high-limit corporate operational account is uncommon. Recommended protocol: have the CFO or treasury director physically attend with the company secretary at a commercial banking centre; if physically impossible, use a Canadian-licensed lawyer or notary to certify identity, sign powers of attorney, and perform independent legal counsel verification on behalf of the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual entity structure: an Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) incorporated in Alberta while the operating group is foreign-controlled and business activities are conducted through a data center colocation platform.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing from the Alberta Corporate Registry; authenticated Articles of Incorporation and all amendments; certified corporate registry search; shareholder register and ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) declaration; group organizational chart; board resolutions appointing signatories; Canadian tax opinion explaining the legal personality and unlimited liability feature of the ULC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital escrow deposit or equity injection by a non-resident parent without audited financial statements for the newly formed ULC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds package comprising the parent's latest audited financial statements, bank reference letter, board resolution for the capital contribution, signed equity subscription agreement, funding-flow breakdown showing transparent wire sequencing, and an interim business case for the Tier-3/4 data center colocation lease operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High velocity of cross-border wire activity (monthly ACH, SWIFT wires overseas) for server-hosting equipment, rack-space lease payments, and bare-metal service disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with colocation tenants; supplier invoices and purchase orders for server racks and network equipment; projected monthly cash-flow model; general ledger reconciliation; treasury management policy and mandates; explanation of normal-course trade settlement, with underlying commercial contracts and customs documentation for imported hardware.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or signatory appears in adverse media, sanctions exposure, politically exposed person (PEP) lists, or resides in a jurisdiction subject to enhanced monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and proof of residential address; professional or independent reference letter from a lawyer/accountant; CV and business-history statement explaining any old sanctions-listing matches; enhanced due diligence questionnaire; combined OFAC/DFATD sanctions screening results; nexus letter from the foreign parent confirming source of wealth. Where a PEP is identified, provide a source-of-wealth statement and maintain enhanced transaction monitoring approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The ULC's pass-through tax classification creates confusion over whether the entity is treated as a disregarded LLC or a separate corporate deposit account customer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canadian tax counsel opinion confirming the ULC's status as a separate Alberta corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); CRA business number (BN), GST/HST registration, and payroll account; tax treaty classification statements if the ULC elects to be treated as a partnership or transparent entity for U.S. tax purposes; bank account mandate expressly confirming the ULC is the account holder and all signatories act in its name.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from a non-resident parent must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's bank to the ULC's commercial bank account in Canada. The receiving bank must be a Canadian clearing member able to settle through Payments Canada's systems. The remittance instruction must identify the beneficiary as the ULC legal entity exactly as registered, include the 12-digit Canadian account CCD transit (institution/transit) if using the Canadian Clearing Identifier, and state the purpose clearly, e.g., 'Equity Contribution / Capital Subscription - Data Center Colocation ULC'. No Canadian Foreign Exchange Administration approval is required. For CAD-denominated capital, same-day finality is achieved through Payments Canada's Lynx; for USD, the cashier-wire settles through the Canadian bank's U.S. correspondent. The bank will require board resolutions, share-issuance documentation, and a funds-flow statement before accepting the first tranche. Any international electronic transfer of CAD 10,000 or more is reported to FINTRAC as an EFT report; the bank reports automatically, but the ULC must retain all underlying transaction records for regulatory and internal audit purposes. If the non-resident parent acquires direct or indirect control of a Canadian business, an Investment Canada Act notification may be required before closing for non-cultural businesses above the threshold; the filing should be prepared independently of banking onboarding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and treasury disbursements from the Alberta ULC operate through standard Canadian clearing rails. Primary rails include: SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for international vendor payments and parent-fund repatriation; SWIFT MT101 bulk transfer files for recurring invoices; Payments Canada ACSS debits/credits for same-country ACH-style settlements; Lynx wire transfer for urgent CAD settlements; and the commercial letter of credit (documentary LC) route via SWIFT MT700 for imported server hardware if suppliers require bank-issued undertakings. Recurring monthly tenant lease collections from Canadian data center clients should use pre-authorized debit agreements cleared through ACSS; cross-border tenant/wire collections should use MT103 or an accredited ACH originator if USD is cleared through the U.S. ACH network. All outbound disbursements require segregation of duties: treasury preparer, checker, and signatory director; reconciliation against the accounting ledger; and retention of supplier contracts, invoices, and delivery documentation for AML and tax audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in CAD/USD and, where commercially needed, CAD/EUR and CAD/GBP, with bona-fide underlying commercial exposure
FX swaps (simultaneous spot/forward or forward/forward exchanges) for temporary cross-border liquidity management with the same clearing counterparty
Cross-currency swaps in CAD/USD, subject to ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and bilateral credit support annex, used to align long-term data center capital expenditures with lease revenues
European-style vanilla FX options (call or put structures) purchased to floor or cap conversion rates on committed capital injections and lease payments

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not prohibited under Canadian law but are uneconomic for CAD due to the liquid onshore forward market; NDFs are permissible only where an onshore deliverable forward cannot be executed by the counterparty, and they must be documented under an enforceable ISDA agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within two months after the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation or registration in Alberta; file annually while active.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in registry notices and administrative dissolution or strike-off. Restoration may require prescribed filings, fees, and evidence of good standing. The standard government fee is approximately CAD 30, subject to exchange rates and registry changes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private Alberta corporation, including an Alberta ULC, generally may dispense with appointing an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution unless its articles, shareholder agreement, financing documents, or another applicable law requires an audit. Public or distributing corporations and entities subject to sector-specific requirements generally require an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for qualifying private entities; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) may be used where elected or required. Financial statements must comply with the Alberta Business Corporations Act and applicable tax requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not generally require an annual public UBO filing for an Alberta private corporation. The corporation must maintain accurate ownership, share-transfer, director, and control records and update them promptly after changes. Beneficial ownership and control information may be required under applicable federal anti-money-laundering, tax, banking, or contractual due-diligence rules. An annual internal confirmation is recommended.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute book containing shareholder and director resolutions and meeting minutes
Articles, amendments, bylaws, and shareholder agreements
Register of individuals with significant control or equivalent beneficial ownership records where legally applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,200 annually for registered-office, records-office, and corporate secretarial support; Alberta does not generally require a separate statutory registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-10,000 for a small private ULC where an audit is required or voluntarily commissioned; no audit fee applies where a valid audit exemption is available and used.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined: Federal Part I 15% + Alberta provincial 8% (non-CCPC ULC)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; preferential items: SR&ED investment tax credit (15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs), 30% refundable Clean Technology ITC for qualifying clean-energy manufacturing/cogeneration assets, accelerated CCA for server equipment (Class 10, 30% DB, enhanced first-year allowance under the Accelerated Investment Incentive); Small Business Deduction NOT available to a ULC controlled by non-residents.
